_comment: Academic/institutional citations backing Trail Mix's CDN relevance. Same discipline as data/sources.json's research_queue, kept separate because these support the funding application and research framing rather than in-game educational text — nothing in trail-mix-v2.html or the trail pages reads this file.
_verification_method: Confirmed via WebSearch returning matching snippets from official uib.no / cdn.uib.no pages (WebFetch to those domains is not reachable from this build environment — the same block that affects snl.no). This is stronger than the original unsourced AI-chat claims, which came with no URLs at all, but it is search-snippet corroboration, not a human reading the full rendered page. Before quoting any of this in a formal application, open each url once and confirm the snippet matches the live page — flagged per-entry as human_check_recommended.

_schema.as_claimed: the original claim as it arrived from the AI chat session, close to verbatim
_schema.confirmed: what a WebSearch pass actually found, with direct quotes where the source snippet provided them
_schema.url: the official uib.no/cdn.uib.no page (or DOI) that confirms it
_schema.verified: true = an official CDN/UiB source was found matching the claim; still subject to human_check_recommended
_schema.verified_by: claude (web search, 2026-08-16) — not a substitute for opening the url

citations.as_claimed: CDN 2025 exhibition 'Game Poems of Place and Encounter'. Described as moving away from conventional objectives toward metaphor, ritual space and rhythm, with walking and traversal as gameplay mechanics tied to pacing and exploration of place. A piece titled 'With Magnus to Norway' is claimed to combine 8-bit aesthetics with a contemplative walk through Norwegian nature.
citations.confirmed: 'Game Poems of Place and Encounter' exhibited at CDN, University of Bergen, 6-20 June 2025. Magnuson is a 2024-25 Fulbright Fellow in Digital Culture at UiB. 'With Magnus to Norway' (2024) is a videogame installation with 8-bit aesthetics and a repurposed dance-pad controller, described as 'a contemplative walk through nature with a growing child, that is simultaneously a journey towards an ancestral homeland' — matches the claim closely.
citations.relevance_if_true: Supports treating walking itself, without conventional objectives, as the game's core mechanic — directly relevant to Trail Mix having no 'reach the summit' scoring.

citations.as_claimed: Professor II in CDN's games node, focus on Transformative Play. Project 'The Witch's Way' described as emerging through an 'embodied dialogue' with the physical place of Gotland, exploring how games can trigger transformative processes around identity, isolation, meaning and purpose.
citations.confirmed: CDN event page: Doris Rusch, 'Finding the Witch's Way — A Story About Embodied Writing and Mattering.' The project is described as an 'embodied dialogue between being claimed by a space (Gotland) and telling its mysteries back to itself,' originating from the question of how games can 'ignite transformative processes related to big, existential questions — death, identity, isolation and, ultimately, purpose and meaning.' Confirmed near-verbatim. She is a professor at Uppsala University and Professor II at CDN.
citations.relevance_if_true: Supports the idea that Bergen's actual terrain (gradient, weather, other walkers) can shape narrative structure rather than just decorate it.

citations.as_claimed: Leads CDN's Computer Games and Interactive Digital Narrative node. Research on player-centred interaction with game interfaces and experience of sound in games; node investigates agency, materiality, interactivity, emotion and immersion.
citations.confirmed: Confirmed node leader of Computer Games and Interactive Digital Narrative at CDN. Node studies 'the intersection between player and game in the shaping of narrative experiences,' the functions of 'agency, materiality, interactivity, and play.' Jørgensen's own interests confirmed as including 'player interaction with game interfaces' and 'player experiences of sound in games' (see her Game Studies article on sound).
citations.relevance_if_true: Supports treating Jack's live set as an interface the player experiences the route through, not background music.

citations.person: Scott Rettberg / Jhave Johnston, XDN and AIR
citations.as_claimed: 'Extending Digital Narrative' (XDN) project uses artistic practice as research method, testing AI/VR/interactive media hands-on. A 2026 paper is claimed: 'Extending Digital Narrative with AI, Games, Chatbots, and XR: How Experimental Creative Practice Yields Research Insights.' Separately, CDN's Artistic Integrated Research (AIR) is claimed to describe using a handheld projector to place hidden digital works in forests, with location-changing narratives.
citations.confirmed: Both claims confirmed independently. The paper exists with that exact title, published 2026, DOI 10.3390/h15010017, Scott Rettberg listed as author. XDN project page confirms Rettberg as PI, exploring 'algorithmic narrativity' through direct engagement with AI and XR. The AIR node page states almost verbatim: 'A hand-held projector can be used to place hidden digital works in forests... software for large game studios can create narratives that change based on location.'
citations.relevance_if_true: The AIR/projector claim is a close, citable precedent for the QR/print trail already built and for any future physical projection work. The paper can be cited directly by DOI.

citations.as_claimed: ALGOFOLK project studies the mutual shaping of everyday creativity and automated systems — not whether machines are creative, but how algorithms shape creative practice and vice versa.
citations.confirmed: Confirmed. Full project name: 'Algorithmic folklore: The mutual shaping of vernacular creativity and automation,' led by Gabriele de Seta at CDN/UiB, funded by a Trond Mohn Foundation Starting Grant (2024-2028). De Seta was previously part of the ERC-funded Machine Vision project. Described as researching 'algorithmic folklore — a new interplay between human creativity and automation.'
citations.relevance_if_true: Gives a citable frame for the distinction already built into data/folklore.json: a being's tradition_source (documented folklore) versus its rendering here (contemporary interpretation).

citations.as_claimed: CDN 2026 seminar 'Daemons, Myths and Monsters'. Rizvi's research described as examining cultural flattening and narrative bias in LLMs, including 'flattened spirits and displaced monsters in GPT stories.' Gunderson's work described as covering AI imaginaries, algorithmic folklore, monstrosity and prompting as relational practice.
citations.confirmed: Confirmed exactly. Official CDN event 'Daemons, Myths, and Monsters: Narratives of technology in the age of artificial intelligence.' Rizvi's talk title matches verbatim: 'Flattened spirits and displaced monsters in GPT stories.' Gunderson's talk: 'Algorithmic monsters: How AI is produced as other and how AI creations are perceived as monstrous.' Rizvi's research area confirmed as 'cultural flattening and narrative bias in LLMs.'
citations.relevance_if_true: The single most load-bearing citation in this file — it means the researchers most likely to review this application study exactly the failure mode a citation list like this one risks. Was checked first and most carefully, as the checklist required.

citations.as_claimed: 'Machine Vision' project studied how algorithmic images and machine-vision technologies affect how people and societies understand the world, including through games, narratives and digital art.
citations.confirmed: Confirmed and more precise than the original claim. Full title: 'Machine Vision in Everyday Life: Playful Interactions with Visual Technologies in Digital Art, Games, Narratives and Social Media,' an ERC Consolidator project (2018-2024), Jill Walker Rettberg as PI. Produced a database of 500 games, artworks and narratives depicting machine vision. Rettberg is Professor of Digital Culture and Co-Director of CDN.
citations.relevance_if_true: Supports the interface pattern already built for the Botanical Garden concept: show the sensor reading (INPUT: SOUND LEVEL) rather than implying the installation understands the visitor.
